summary.headline: The Southborough School Committee reviewed town guidelines and timelines for the FY28 budget and began drafting district budget priorities.
summary.summary: District administrators presented the FY28 budget calendar and preparation process under guidance from the Select Board, which requires submitting both a level-service budget and a level-funded budget. The committee reviewed several budget variables, including special education tuition, energy inflation, and potential operational costs linked to the Neary elementary building project. Members also refined a draft list of FY28 budget priorities, agreeing to extend the district capital planning outlook from five years to eight to ten years.

topics.title: FY28 budget process and timeline
topics.summary: District administration outlined the instructions, variables, and schedule for assembling the FY28 school operating budget. The town requested that departments prepare two models: a level-service budget with identified efficiencies and a level-funded budget holding non-salary expenses to FY27 amounts with no new positions or programs.
key_details: Special education out-of-district tuition and energy costs remain major volatile variables, while in-house special education transportation offers better predictability.
The superintendent noted potential operational costs associated with moving grades during the proposed Neary elementary building project could impact FY28 or FY29.
Southborough public school budget increases have averaged 3.02 percent over the past 10 years, with FY25 seeing a spike of 5.18 percent due to expiring federal pandemic grants.
School budget spreadsheets were distributed to principals on September 24 and are due back to the finance director on October 20.
The preliminary FY28 budget will be presented to the School Committee on November 9, followed by a recommended budget presentation on January 13, 2027.
topics.outcome: District leaders will prepare level-service and level-funded budget scenarios alongside a five-year projection.
topics.why_it_matters: The budget sets funding levels for local elementary and middle schools, directly influencing taxpayer appropriations, staffing levels, and educational programming.

topics.title: Draft FY28 budget priorities
topics.summary: The committee conducted a first reading of the draft FY28 budget priorities, which provide strategic guidance to administrators during budget preparation. Members discussed protecting core educational programs, managing healthcare and special education costs, tracking grant sustainability, and expanding long-range capital planning.
key_details: Priorities include maintaining class size policies, student well-being, and instructional programs like world languages, health, and science.
The committee emphasized ensuring grant-funded initiatives, such as the PRISM grant, build lasting staff capacity after grant funding expires.
Administrators noted ongoing collaboration with town officials to review healthcare plan designs under state law sections 21 and 22 to achieve mutual savings.
Members agreed to revise the capital planning priority to establish an eight-to-ten year plan rather than a five-year outlook.
topics.outcome: Administrators will update the draft priorities for a second reading at the committee's October 14 meeting.

topics.title: Town Government Study Committee survey inquiry
topics.summary: A committee member asked whether the School Committee as a board had been omitted from receiving an email survey distributed in September by the Town Government Study Committee. Members clarified that some received it individually or through municipal channels, and the chair agreed to confirm distribution.
key_details: The survey regarding town government structure was sent to municipal boards around September 11.
A member noted the School Committee appeared to be missing from the committee distribution list.
topics.outcome: The chair agreed to verify whether the School Committee received the survey.
